reviews.notes: 整体可发布。译文没有按英文句序硬搬，很多地方做了自然的中文重组，例如“能撑规模的技术栈”“长成一门独立的新手艺”“分而治之”等，语气也保留了作者技术但带个人判断的表达。MDX/frontmatter 与代码块结构未见破损；`translationStatus: machine` 保持不作为质量问题。

ignoredIssues.problem: The explanatory code comments remain in English: “Simply print the content”, “Use Text-to-Speech to vocalise the content”, and “Convert content into animated video”. They are reader-facing tutorial comments rather than identifiers, so the Chinese article would read more complete if they were translated.
ignoredIssues.suggestion: Translate the comments while preserving class and method names, e.g. `# 直接打印内容`, `# 使用 Text-to-Speech 朗读内容`, `# 将内容转换成动画视频`.

issues.problem: The title is readable and faithful, but `能撑规模的……` is slightly unfinished-sounding in Chinese because the source truncation already follows an adjective list. It is acceptable, but a smoother house-style title could avoid the dangling `的`.
issues.suggestion: Consider `Berlayar：搭一套稳定、易扩展、灵活、可规模化的……` or keep current if preserving the casual tone is preferred.

reviews.notes: The translation passes: the main prose reads like natural Mandarin technical essay writing rather than sentence-by-sentence calque, preserves Ernie’s casual technical voice, keeps product/code terms intact, and the MDX/frontmatter structure is not broken. The remaining issues are minor polish only.

ignoredIssues.problem: Three explanatory Python comments remain in English: "Simply print the content", "Use Text-to-Speech to vocalise the content", and "Convert content into animated video". These are reader-facing comments inside a teaching snippet, so Chinese readers would benefit from translated comments while preserving code identifiers.
ignoredIssues.suggestion: Translate the comments to Chinese, e.g. `# 直接打印内容`, `# 使用 Text-to-Speech 朗读内容`, `# 将内容转换成动画视频`.
